sentences.text:
Bench: Surepalli Nanda
 Hon'Ble Mrs Justice Surepalli Nanda
 Writ Petition No.17758 of 2023
Order:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Irrigation and Command
Area Development appearing for respondent No.1, learned Government Pleader for Finance and
Planning Depa

rtment appearing for respondent No.2 and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.3 and 4.
2.

The grievance of the petitioner in this writ petition is that in spite of Competent Civil Court passing a judgment and decree, dated 31.05.2011 in L.A.O.P.No.21 of 2008 and the petitioner filing E.P.No.4 of 2023 on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet, the judgement debtor i.e..,
respondent No.4 failed to deposit the decretal amount even after lapse of more than twelve years and the said E.P is being adjourned from time to time.
3.

The facts of the case are that the land in Survey No.170/A2 situated at Makthal Village and Mandal, WP_17758_2023 SN,J Mahabubnagar District, was acquired by Land Acquisition officer,
by passing an Award, dated 06.02.2008 and on the request made by the petitioner herein, the same was referred to the Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act, 1894').
Considering the said reference, the Civil Court passed a judgment and decree, dated 31.05.2011, enhancing the compensation and the same was modified in LAAS No.756 of 2011.

Seeking execution of the said judgment and decree as modified,
the petitioner herein filed E.P.No.4 of 2023 on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet.
In the said E.P., respondent No.4 herein stated to have entered appearance and the said execution proceedings are being dragged on from time to time and are still pending.
Respondent No.4 herein failed to deposit the decretal amount in spite of the said judgment and decree having become final.

Aggrieved by the said inaction on the part of respondent No.4 and the action of respondent Nos.1 and 2 in making available the required funds for complying with the said judgment and decree, the present writ petition is filed.

Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition brings on record the written instructions vide Lr.No.F/32/2021, dated 10.07.2023 and in particular relevant portion of said written instructions Kurva Pedda Laxmanna Died Per Lr vs The State Of Telangana on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146818574/
1 reads as under:
"In this regard this Office submitted the Decretal charges proposals for LAOP No.17/2008 & batch an amount of Rs.4,64,73,810/- (In words Rupees Four Crores Sixty four lakhs Seventy three thousand Eight hundred and ten only) to the District Collector, Narayanpet.

sentences.text: The District Collector, Narayanpet recommended to the Chief Commissioner, Land Administration, Hyderabad.
The Chief Commissioner, Land Administration, Hyderabad recommended to the Spl.
Chief Secretary
Govt. I & CAD (LA) Department vide Lr.No.CCLA-LA-1/LAS1/20/2023-LA-1 dated 27.05.2023.

At present the file is under process in Principle Secretary Irrigation Secretariat,
Hyderabad Telangana for issue G.O Rt and Sanction of Budget.
Soon after received the amount the same is deposit in Civil Court, Narayanpet for compliance court orders."

5. Having, taken note of the facts and circumstances of the case, especially, the fact that the property of the petitioner was acquired, as early as, in the year 2007 and the petitioner was deprived of her property without fixing the proper compensation and though proper compensation was fixed by WP_17758_2023 SN,J the competent Civil Court on reference under Section 18 of the Act, 1894, as early as on 31.05.2011, the petitioner is not being paid with said compensation as of date i.e., even after lapse of more than twelve years, and in the light of law laid down by this Court in the case of Bhamidipati Annaporna Bhavani v. Land Acquisition Officer1 holding that the writ petition is maintainable even when execution proceedings are pending seeking a direction for payment of compensation as fixed by the reference Court, this Court is left with no other option except to declare that the action on the part of the respondents is totally arbitrary, illegal and violative of Article 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.

sentences.text: 6. In the circumstances, the Writ Petition is allowed directing the respondents to deposit the entire decretal amount covered by judgment and decree in L.A.O.P.No.21 of 2008, dated 31.05.2011, into the credit of the E.P.No.4 of 2023 on the file of the Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet, within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

entities.label: COURT

It is made clear that any negligence on the part of the respondents in complying with this order within the time stipulated will be viewed seriously and in such an event, the respondents would be liable to pay heavy costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Aggrieved by the said inaction on the part of respondent No.4 and the action of respondent Nos.1 and 2 in making available the required funds for complying with the said judgment and decree, the present writ petition is filed.
5. Having, taken note of the facts and circumstances of the case, especially, the fact that the property of the petitioner was acquired, as early as, in the year 2007 and the petitioner was deprived of her property without fixing the proper compensation and though proper compensation was fixed by WP_17758_2023 SN,J the competent Civil Court on reference under Section 18 of the Act, 1894, as early as on 31.05.2011, the petitioner is not being paid with said compensation as of date i.e., even after lapse of more than twelve years, and in the light of law laid down by this Court in the case of Bhamidipati Annaporna Bhavani v. Land Acquisition Officer1 holding that the writ petition is maintainable even when execution proceedings are pending seeking a direction for payment of compensation as fixed by the reference Court, this Court is left with no other option except to declare that the action on the part of the respondents is totally arbitrary, illegal and violative of Article 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.
6. In the circumstances, the Writ Petition is allowed directing the respondents to deposit the entire decretal amount covered by judgment and decree in L.A.O.P.No.21 of 2008, dated 31.05.2011, into the credit of the E.P.No.4 of 2023 on the file of the Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet, within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
It is made clear that any negligence on the part of the respondents in complying with this order within the time stipulated will be viewed seriously and in such an event, the respondents would be liable to pay heavy costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
